extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance on provisional/nonstatutory double patenting rejections, determination of patent term filing date, and the proper form, content, and handling of terminal disclaimers (including required form paragraphs and example language). Geared toward examination and prosecution actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term filing date for original utility/plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent term filing date of an original utility or plant application filed on or after June 8, 1995 is the earliest of: (a) the actual filing date of the application; or (b) the filing date of the earliest application for which the application claims the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an original patent application has no specific reference to any earlier-filed application under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c), the patent term filing date is the date the application was actually filed. Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f), 365(a) or (b), or 386(a) or (b) are not taken into account when determining the term of an issued patent and thus not in determining the patent term filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application patent term filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent term filing date of a reissue application for purposes of nonstatutory double patenting analysis is the patent term filing date of the original application that resulted in the patent for which reissue is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the original application's patent term filing date when performing double patenting analyses on reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection — earlier patent term filing date (examiner action)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection is the only rejection remaining in an application having the earlier patent term filing date, the examiner should withdraw the rejection in the application having the earlier patent term filing date and permit that application to issue as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting the earlier application to issue will convert the provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection in the other application into a nonstatutory double patenting rejection upon issuance of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection — same patent term filing date (examiner action and applicant remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: If both the application under examination and the reference application have the same patent term filing date, the provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection made in each application should be maintained until it is overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejections are subject to 37 CFR 1.111(b). Applicant can overcome such a rejection by filing a reply that either shows the claims are patentably distinct from the claims of the reference application or by filing a terminal disclaimer in the application under 37 CFR 1.321 that obviates the rejection. If the reply is sufficient, the examiner will withdraw the rejection in the application in which it was submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection — later patent term filing date (examiner action)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection is the only rejection remaining in an application, and that application has the later patent term filing date, the rejection should be maintained until applicant overcomes the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to overcome the rejection follow the same approaches noted for same-date situations (show patentable distinctness or submit a compliant terminal disclaimer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action after Board decision not reaching provisional rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board does not include an opinion on a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection but reverses other grounds as to a claim rejected based on provisional nonstatutory double patenting, and the applicant has not filed a proper terminal disclaimer, the examiner must act upon the provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must determine if any reference application used in the provisional rejection has issued as a patent. If it has issued, re-issue the provisional rejection as a nonprovisional rejection and require a terminal disclaimer (use appropriate form paragraphs). If the reference application has been abandoned or has not matured to a patent and the provisional double patenting rejection is the only remaining rejection, the examiner should withdraw the provisional rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design applications: patent term and double patenting handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications, patent term is measured from the issue date; determination of patent term filing date is not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a provisional double patenting rejection (statutory or nonstatutory) is the only rejection remaining in the earlier application, the examiner should withdraw that rejection and permit that application to issue as a patent. If both conflicting design applications were filed on the same date, maintain the provisional double patenting rejection in each until overcome. For double patenting analysis involving applications filed prior to June 8, 1995, or design/utility conflicts, examiners should consult their TQAS or SPE to determine whether provisional rejections should be withdrawn or not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to notify status of terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs (¶ 14.23 et seq.) are provided to inform the applicant or patent owner of the status of a submitted terminal disclaimer (e.g., accepted, not accepted, reexamination-specific variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph (14.23 for proper terminal disclaimer; 14.23.01 for reexamination; 14.24–14.32 for improper disclaimers). Follow examiner notes for insertion of bracketed fields (dates, patent/application numbers) and for selection of reexamination-specific paragraphs. Certain paragraphs must be preceded or followed by specified paragraphs (see sequencing rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer compliance with 37 CFR 1.321 (general requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer must comply with 37 CFR 1.321; noncompliance grounds include failure to state extent of interest, being directed to particular claim(s), not being signed, failure to identify the application/patent being disclaimed, and failure to submit the disclaimer fee or authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See form paragraphs 14.26 (sub-heading) and 14.26.01–14.26.10 for specific failures: 14.26.01 Extent of interest not stated (37 CFR 1.321(b)(3)); 14.26.02 directed to particular claim(s) (disclaimer must be of the terminal portion of the entire patent); 14.26.03 not signed; 14.26.04 application/patent not identified (do not use for apps filed on/after Sept 16, 2012); 14.26.07 no disclaimer fee submitted (cite 37 CFR 1.20(d)); 14.26.08 & 14.26.09 & 14.26.10 address signatory and identification issues for filings on or after Sept. 16, 2012 and before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of interest must be stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who has signed the disclaimer must state the extent of the applicant's or assignee’s interest in the application/patent (37 CFR 1.321(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extent of interest is not stated, use form paragraph 14.26.01 (and it MUST be preceded by the introductory paragraphs 14.24/14.25 and 14.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must not be directed to particular claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer directed to a particular claim or claims is not acceptable since the disclaimer must be of the terminal portion of the term of the entire patent to be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If so directed, use form paragraph 14.26.02 and precede it with form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 and 14.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and signatory capacity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer must be properly signed. For applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, the signer must be the applicant, the patentee, or an attorney or agent of record and must state the capacity in which they sign; for applications filed before that date, all owners may need to sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not signed or signatory capacity not stated, use form paragraphs 14.26.03 (not signed), 14.26.06.fti (not signed by all owners for pre-Sept.16,2012), and 14.26.09 (failure to state capacity for on/after Sept.16,2012). Paragraph 14.26.08 addresses improper signer for applications filed on or after Sept.16,2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/patent being disclaimed must be identified correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: The application/patent being disclaimed must be identified; improper or missing identification is a ground of noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.26.04 if not identified (do not use for applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012). Use 14.26.05 when the identification number is incorrect — insert correct number and note that a terminal disclaimer may still be acceptable if it includes correct number and proper filing date/series code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer fee must be submitted or authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclaimer fee required by 37 CFR 1.20(d) must be submitted or there must be authorization to charge a Deposit Account or credit card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no fee submitted, use form paragraph 14.26.07 and insert the fee amount in bracketed field. If a disclaimer fee was paid for a terminal disclaimer which was not accepted, the previously submitted disclaimer fee will be applied when a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer is submitted (do not use 14.26.07 in that case). Form paragraph 14.35 may inform applicant the previously submitted fee will be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party identified in disclaimer must be applicant of record (post-Sept.16,2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, the party identified in the terminal disclaimer must be the applicant of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not the applicant, a request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c) must be filed including an application data sheet specifying the applicant and complying with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73; to be reconsidered the terminal disclaimer must be filed with the request under 37 CFR 1.46(c). Use form paragraph 14.26.10 to notify applicant of this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must include clause enforceable only during period of common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer must include a recitation that any patent granted shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patent is commonly owned with the application(s) or patent(s) which formed the basis for the double patenting rejection (37 CFR 1.321(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this clause is missing, use form paragraph 14.27.01 (must be preceded by form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 and 14.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Research Agreement (JRA) / 37 CFR 1.321(d) statement required when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: When the terminal disclaimer is based on activities undertaken within the scope of a joint research agreement (affecting 35 U.S.C. 102(c) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2)&(3)), it must include the waiver and enforceability provisions of 37 CFR 1.321(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically it must: (1) waive the right to separately enforce any patent granted on that application (or being reexamined) and the reference patent (or any patent granted on the reference application) and (2) agree that any patent granted shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patents are not separately enforced. Use form paragraph 14.27.011 and follow sequencing rules (preceded by 14.24/14.25 and 14.26). For pre- and post-Sept.16,2012 differences see examiner notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to disclaim terminal portion of any patent granted on subject application or of subject patent (remedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the terminal disclaimer fails to disclaim the terminal portion of any patent granted on the subject application, or fails to disclaim the terminal portion of the subject patent (reexamination/reissue contexts), the examiner must notify applicant and provide examples of proper language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 14.27.02 and 14.27.03 as appropriate; when using these, give an example of proper terminal disclaimer language using form paragraphs 14.27.04/14.27.04.1 (application-filed-before/after Sept.16,2012) or 14.27.06 for reexamination situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of acceptable terminal disclaimer language (templates and forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP provides model language for acceptable terminal disclaimers in various situations (provisional nonstatutory double patenting over a pending application; nonstatutory double patenting over a reference patent; reexamination situations; joint research agreements), with variants for applications filed before and on/after Sept. 16, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include full sample paragraphs that (a) disclaim the terminal portion of the statutory term which would extend beyond expiration of the reference patent/application, (b) include agreement that any patent so granted shall be enforceable only during common ownership, and (c) declare the waiver to separately enforce. The guidance notes alternative use of official forms (Form PTO/SB/25, PTO/SB/26, PTO/AIA/25, PTO/AIA/26, PTO/SB/25a, PTO/SB/26a, PTO/AIA forms) and references to which example to use depending on filing date and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer language must run with the patent and bind successors/assigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer and the waiver/agreement shall run with any patent granted on the instant application and be binding upon the grantee/applicant/patentee, its successors or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample language in form paragraphs explicitly states this (included in examples for both pre- and post-Sept.16,2012 filings and for reexamination situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph sequencing and mandatory precedences
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs for improper terminal disclaimers MUST be preceded by the introductory form paragraph(s) (14.24 or 14.25) and form paragraph 14.26 before being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many specific deficiency paragraphs state: 'This form paragraph MUST be preceded by form paragraph 14.24 or 14.25 AND form paragraph 14.26.' Examiners should follow the sequencing and use the appropriate follow-up paragraphs (14.26.01 to 14.27.03 etc.) and use 14.35 when informing applicant about fee application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the correct form paragraphs in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Different (or variant) form paragraphs exist for reexamination proceedings (e.g., 14.23.01, 14.25 for reexamination), and examiners must select reexamination-specific paragraphs where indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use non-reexamination paragraphs in reexamination contexts; follow examiner notes which indicate which paragraphs are reexamination-only and which are not to be used in reexamination proceedings.
